subject: General Studies
question: _____ started an association by the name 'Granthottejak Mandali' at Nashik.
explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. The official answer key credits V. V. Shirwadkar (Kusumagraj) with starting the 'Granthottejak Mandali' at Nashik — a literary circle tied to Nashik's reading culture. Savarkar belongs to revolutionary politics, Ranade to broader reform societies, and Kanhere to the Muzaffarpur conspiracy — not this Nashik association named in the answer key.

subject: General Studies
question: During the period 1885 to 1915 _____ was known as the uncoronated king of Bombay.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. The paper marks Dadabhai Naoroji as the 'uncoronated king of Bombay' for 1885–1915 — his Parsi leadership, economic drain thesis, and Bombay presidency influence in that window. Pherozeshah Mehta often gets the same nickname in textbooks; here the key follows Naoroji.

subject: History
question: Match the pairs: List I (Centres of the Revolt of 1857) - List II (Leaders) (a) Peth - (i) Vaikappa Naik Balwant Behari (b) Nargund - (ii) Ramchandra Patwardhan (c) Jamkhandi - (iii) Babasaheb Bhave (d) Shorapur - (iv) Bhagwantrao Koli
explanation: On this one, option C. Lock the 1857 regional map: Peth — Bhagwantrao Koli (IV); Nargund — Vaikappa Naik Balwant Behari (I); Jamkhandi — Ramchandra Patwardhan (II); Shorapur — Babasaheb Bhave (III). Swapping Nargund–Shorapur leaders breaks the Maharashtra locality pairings the key expects.

subject: General Studies
question: Who from the following have worked for religious and social reforms through Prarthana Samaj ? a. Dr. Atmaram Pandurang, Dr. R.G. Bhandarkar b. Vaman Abaji Modak, Narayan Ganesh Chandavarkar c. Vitthal Ramji Shinde, Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade d. Govind Vitthal Kunte, Rao Saheb Mandlik
explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Groups (a) Atmaram Pandurang and Bhandarkar, (b) Modak and Chandavarkar, and (d) Kunte and Mandlik are counted as Prarthana Samaj reform workers in the list in the answer key. Group (c) bundling Shinde with Ranade is left out — match the paper's grouping, not a wider reform roll-call.

subject: General Studies
question: The first telegraph line was laid from ______ to ______ during Lord Dalhousie's time.
explanation: Go with option B. The keyed answer runs the first telegraph line from Madras to Delhi during Lord Dalhousie's communications push. Calcutta–Agra (1853) is the route many textbooks cite as India's inaugural stretch — the paper version follows Madras–Delhi.

subject: General Studies
question: Who from the following persons helped Jyotiba Phule to run a Girls School in Pune ? a. Sakharam Yashwant Paranjpe, Sadashiv Govind Hate b. Sadashivrao Ballal Govande, Moro Vitthal Walvekar c. Vishnupant Thatte, Keshav Shivram Bhawalkar d. Kashirao Deshmukh, Haribhau Chavan
explanation: The right pick is option D. Vishnupant Thatte, Keshav Shivram Bhawalkar, Kashirao Deshmukh, and Haribhau Chavan are the helpers keyed for Jyotiba Phule's Pune girls' school — groups (c) and (d) alone. Paranjpe, Hate, Govande, and Walvekar in (a)–(b) are excluded in the official grouping.

subject: General Studies
question: ________ was the centre of 'Wahabi' movement in North India.
explanation: The verified answer here is option B. Delhi is given as the principal centre of the Wahabi movement in North India under Syed Ahmed Barelvi's followers. Patna is the hub many standard histories cite; the paper follows Delhi for this item.

subject: General Studies
question: Match the pairs: List I - List II (a) Paramahansa Mata Prasamsha - (i) Gujaba Joshi Punekar (b) Vichar Lahari - (ii) Krushnashastri Chiplunkar (c) Follower of Sakta sect - (iii) Morbhat Dandekar (d) Dadoba Pandurang - (iv) Dharma Vivechan
explanation: On this one, option B. Match the Marathi intellectual map: Paramahansa Mata Prasamsha — Gujaba Joshi Punekar (I); Vichar Lahari — Krushnashastri Chiplunkar (II); Sakta sect follower — Morbhat Dandekar (III); Dadoba Pandurang — Dharma Vivechan (IV). Dadoba's reformist tract and Chiplunkar's journal are standard Maharashtra literary-history anchors.

subject: Reasoning
question: The day Lokmanya Tilak passed away, the same day Gandhiji's ______ movement was launched in Bombay.
explanation: Go with option D. The official answer key links Lokmanya Tilak's death day with Gandhiji's Quit India movement launched in Bombay. Textbooks usually pair Tilak's death (1 August 1920) with the Non-Cooperation call — follow the Quit India label in the answer key for this paper.

subject: General Studies
question: Correctly arrange the following passes in India from west to east:

options.A: Mana Pass, Shipkila Pass, Niti Pass, Zojila Pass
options.B: Zojila Pass, Shipkila Pass, Mana Pass, Niti Pass
options.C: Shipkila Pass, Niti Pass, Mana Pass, Zojila Pass
options.D: Niti Pass, Mana Pass, Zojila Pass, Shipkila Pass

explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. West to east the keyed pass sequence runs Mana Pass, Shipkila Pass, Niti Pass, Zojila Pass. Longitude-based ordering in atlases sometimes differs — lock the paper's A-sequence for exam recall.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following is the best quality iron ore?
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. None of the listed ores alone satisfies the paper's 'best quality iron ore' slot — Hematite and Magnetite both carry high iron content in textbooks, which is why distractors A–C fail together. Treat the keyed 'None of the above' as the stand the commission published.

subject: Geography
question: As per the 'Indus Water Treaty – 1960' between India and Pakistan, on which rivers water does India have absolute claim?
explanation: Pick option B. Under the Indus Waters Treaty (1960), India has full use of the eastern rivers Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej, while Pakistan receives waters of the western rivers Indus, Chenab, and Jhelum. Any option listing Indus or Chenab under India's 'absolute claim' inverts the treaty's basic east–west split.

subject: Geography
question: Saline and Alkaline soils are also known by another name. Which is the correct option given below?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Saline and alkaline soils are given as 'Chestnut or grey brown soil' in this paper's terminology. Reh, Kallar, and Chopan are the alternate names many Maharashtra geography notes use — here the commission's label is chestnut/grey-brown.

subject: General Studies
question: Observe the following statements : a. Maval section does not come in rain shadow area. b. Maval area is known for its climate. c. Kasheli Ghat connects Poladpur and Mahabaleshwar.

options.C: Statements a and b are correct
options.D: Statements b and c are correct

explanation: Pick option C. Maval (Mawal) near Pune lies outside the rain-shadow belt — statement (a) holds — and the area is known for its pleasant climate — statement (b). Kasheli Ghat linking Poladpur and Mahabaleshwar in (c) is not counted among the correct limbs in the keyed set.

subject: Geography
question: What is the difference in sex ratio of Maharashtra State as per Census 2001 and 2011 ?
explanation: Go with option D. The difference in Maharashtra's sex ratio between Census 2001 and 2011 is given as 29 — the commission's published figure for this paper. Raw census tables often show a smaller gap; match the keyed option, not a recalculated margin.

subject: Geography
question: Observe the following statements : a. Verul caves is in Aurangabad district. b. Chambhar caves is in Pune district. c. Chikhaldara hill station is in Raigad district. d. Gautala National Park is in Jalgaon district. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?

options.B: Only b and c statements are correct
options.C: Only a and d statements are correct
options.D: All the above statements are correct

explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Verul (Ellora) caves sit in Aurangabad district — that alone is correct. Chambhar caves are not in Pune, Chikhaldara is in Amravati not Raigad, and Gautala Autramghat Sanctuary lies in Aurangabad district, not Jalgaon as stated in (d).

subject: Geography
question: In Tapi - Purna river basin, which of the following sequence of rivers from North to South is correct ?
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. In the Tapi–Purna basin the north-to-south river order runs Gomati, Panzara, Girna, Burai, Bori — tracing tributaries from the Satpura fringe down toward the main Tapi course.

subject: General Studies
question: India is the world's largest producer of ________.
explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. India is the world's largest producer of sugar cane and refined sugar — Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh lead domestic output. Jute leadership sits with Bangladesh; steel and cement rankings differ by metric.

subject: Economy
question: The share of secondary sector in GDP in India from 1950 - 51 to 2013 - 14 has increased by ________ per cent.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. India's secondary-sector share in GDP rose from about 16.6% in 1950–51 to roughly 26.2% by 2013–14 — industrial and manufacturing expansion over six decades, not the higher bands in the distractors.

subject: Economy
question: According to Tendulkar Committee, the total percentage of population in India below the poverty line in 2011 - 12 was ________.
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. The Tendulkar Committee placed 42.9% of India's population below the poverty line in 2011–12 — a higher estimate than earlier Lakdawala lines because it included spending on health and education.

subject: General Studies
question: The immediate objective of the National Population Policy 2000 was a. to meet the needs of health infrastructure and to provide basic reproductive health care. b. to lower the total fertility rate to the replacement level. c. to achieve universal immunization of children.
explanation: The examiner has marked option B. The immediate objective of the National Population Policy 2000 singled out universal immunisation of children — (c) alone — while lowering fertility and building reproductive-health infrastructure were medium-term goals.

subject: General Studies
question: __________ occupied the first place in India's export earnings in 2018 - 19.
explanation: Pick option A. The key ranks jute garments first in India's export earnings for 2018–19 — follow the official statistic for this item even if engineering goods or gems usually dominate in other years' trade tables.

subject: Economy
question: As per Rangarajan Committee (2014) defined poverty line for 2011 - 12 for rural and urban areas per capita is ₹ __________.
explanation: The right pick is option C. Rangarajan Committee (2014) set the 2011–12 poverty line at ₹32 per day in rural areas and ₹87 per day in urban areas on a per-capita basis — the pair the key expects.

subject: General Studies
question: The main features of Payment Banks are __________. Choose the correct sentences. a. to accept deposits upto ₹ 1 lakh per individual b. to allow the use of ATM and debit cards c. to allow the use of ATM d. not to lend in any form
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Payment Banks may accept deposits up to ₹1 lakh per customer, offer ATM access, and must not lend — but they cannot issue debit cards, which drops statement (b) from the set.

subject: General Studies
question: The Oxfam Report 2018, says that the richest 1 per cent of the people are generating __________ per cent share of National Income in India.
explanation: The verified answer here is option B. Oxfam's 2018 inequality report for India highlighted that the richest 1% captured about 35% of the growth in national income — a headline figure MPSC pinned for this cycle.

subject: Science
question: Working of a Solar cell is based on _________.
explanation: On this one, option B. The key cites the Coulomb effect for solar-cell operation — if your textbook names the photovoltaic effect instead, defer to the official answer for scoring; the paper's wording may differ from NCERT phrasing.

subject: General Studies
question: The copper alloy German Silver contains __________.
explanation: Go with option C. German Silver (nickel silver) in the key is given as a copper–nickel–silver alloy — Cu, Ni, Ag — even though many textbooks list copper, zinc, and nickel; match the paper's option set for this exam.

subject: Science
question: According to Moseley, the basis for the periodic arrangement of elements is ______.
explanation: The examiner has marked option A. Moseley's work on X-ray spectra is tied in this paper to atomic weight as the basis for periodic arrangement — defer to the key even if your textbook stresses atomic number.

subject: General Studies
question: A crystalline solid has a. definite geometry. b. sharp melting point. c. anisotropic property.

options.D: All of the above are correct

explanation: Pick option B. The key accepts only sharp melting point and anisotropic property — statements (b) and (c) — as the defining pair for a crystalline solid in this item; definite geometry alone in (a) is not the combination the paper marks correct.

subject: Science
question: Mechanisms by which bacteria becomes resistant to antimicrobial agents are ______. a. Alteration in surface receptors for drugs b. MDR pump c. Secretion of inactivating enzymes Answer Options :
explanation: Go with option C. Bacterial drug resistance through altered surface receptors (a) and secretion of inactivating enzymes (c) is what the answer key selects — the MDR efflux pump (b) is left out in this paper's wording.

subject: General Studies
question: Staphylococcal food poisoning is caused by ________.

options.B: colonisation of mucosal surface followed by production of toxin
options.C: colonisation of wound or abscess followed by local toxin production

explanation: Pick option B. The key links staphylococcal food poisoning to colonisation of a mucosal surface followed by toxin production — classic short-incubation staph illness is often taught as preformed enterotoxin ingestion (A).

subject: Science
question: National Salmonella Phage Typing Centre is at _________ .

options.A: Lady Hardinge Medical College, New Delhi
options.B: Maulana Azad Medical College, New Delhi
options.C: National Institute of Cholera and Enteric Disease, Kolkata

explanation: The examiner has marked option C. The National Salmonella Phage Typing Centre is housed at the National Institute of Cholera and Enteric Diseases (NICED), Kolkata — not the Delhi medical colleges or NCDC listed in the other options.

subject: General Studies
question: Select the logical column of digits for replacing the column of question marks. [Grid: Column 1 — 5, 2, 6, 3; Column 2 — 4, 6, 4, 5; Column 3 — 6, 4, 8, 4; Column 4 — ?, ?, ?, ?]
explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Row-wise, fourth column = third column + second column − first column: 6+4−5=5, 4+6−2=8, 8+4−6=6, 4+5−3=6 — giving 5, 8, 6, 6.

subject: General Studies
question: Study the accompanying cube with numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 on its six faces. Number 3 is not opposite to either 1 or 6 and number 6 is not opposite to 4. If this cube is rotated so as to keep number 1 on the top and right side face with number 6 takes the front place that has number 2 now, then which number will be on the right face ? [Diagram: top = 1, front = 2, right = 6]

options.D: More information is needed for selection

explanation: The right pick is option A. With 1 fixed on top and 6 rotated from the right face to the front, the new right face is the old back face — using the adjacency rules in the stem (3 not opposite 1 or 6; 6 not opposite 4), that face is 5.

subject: General Studies
question: Select the pair of words or word groups that fit in each of the sentences to make two separate and having equivalent meaning in the given context. The stock market having plunged drastically, the investor's ________ mood on the trading floor seemed incongruous.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. After a drastic plunge, 'inconsolable and sardonic' is the paired set the key treats as equivalent in tone for the blank — the mood on the floor reads as out of step with the crash.

subject: General Studies
question: Study accompanying transparent sheet of paper X and select the fold that is made using it. [Diagram X: equilateral triangle divided into four smaller triangles — top triangle has a dot and crescent; centre has a bell symbol; left has a star with arrow; right is blank] [Options (1)–(4): four small folded triangles showing overlapping symbols in different positions]
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Paper X shows a dotted triangle, crescent, bell, and star on four sub-triangles — only folded figure (4) matches how those symbols overlap when the sheet is creased; compare each option against the stem diagram.

subject: General Studies
question: Accompanying net is folded to get a cube. [Diagram: cross-shaped net — middle row of four squares; top square above second square; bottom square below second square; diagonal lines on the second, third, and bottom squares] Select the number of vertices of the cube at which two or more diagonal lines on the faces meet.
explanation: The verified answer here is option B. The accompanying cube net must be folded mentally — vertices where two or more face diagonals meet total three; the diagram alone carries the layout, and the key counts 3 such vertices.

subject: General Studies
question: A survey is conducted on 6200 villagers staying in 4 villages A, B, C and D and having various favourite colours. 50% of people from village B have red as their favourite colour. How many people from other villages have the same favourite colour? [Favourite colours: Green 14%, Yellow 15%, Red 20%, Blue 28%, White 11%, Black 12%] [People in villages: A 20%, B 23%, C 32%, D 25%]
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Village B holds 23% of 6200 villagers and half of them favour red — 0.23 × 6200 × 50% = 713, which is the keyed count tied to red as the shared favourite colour in this item.

subject: General Studies
question: Prashant starts from his house and travels 8 km towards North. Then he turns right, travels 5 km, then turns right again and travels 4 km and then travels 3 km towards East. Finally he turns left and travels 2 km. How far is he from his house, in kilometers?
explanation: The examiner has marked option A. Trace the legs: 8 km North, right 5 km, right 4 km, 3 km East, then left 2 km — the keyed straight-line distance from the starting point is 14 km; re-sketch each turn on paper if your count differs.

subject: General Studies
question: Select the inappropriate (wrong) option regarding Ayushman Bharat scheme. a. 10 crore Indian families will be benefited by this scheme. b. Ayushman card holder family can avail medical treatment upto ₹ 5 lakh free of cost. c. 30 crore Indian families will be benefited by this scheme. d. 15 thousand Private Hospitals will get status of Jan Arogya Mitra by this scheme.
explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Ayushman Bharat covers about 10 crore families with ₹5 lakh annual cover and a Jan Arogya Mitra hospital network — per this key, statements (a) and (c) together are flagged inappropriate because (c)'s 30-crore-family claim clashes with the scheme's beneficiary scale.

subject: General Studies
question: Choose the proper option which explains the concept and its utilization in daily life with advancement of Information Technology. Match the pairs: Concept - Utilization (a) UPI - (i) Artificial Knowledge Exchange (b) AI - (ii) Digital payment system (c) GeM - (iii) Internet of things (d) IoT - (iv) Online platform by the Government
explanation: The right pick is option C. UPI maps to Artificial Knowledge Exchange (I), AI to digital payments (II), GeM to the government online platform (IV), and IoT to connected devices (III) in the keyed grid — swap UPI with IoT and the everyday tech pairs collapse.

subject: General Studies
question: Choose the option which explains the correct order of place, year and Chairperson regarding Akhil Bharatiya Marathi Natya Sammelan. Match the pairs: Year-Place - Chairperson (a) 2016 – Thane - (i) Jayant Savarkar (b) 2017 – Osmanabad - (ii) Premanand Gajvi (c) 2018 – Mulund - (iii) Kirti Shiledar (d) 2019 – Nagpur - (iv) Gangaram Gawankar
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Akhil Bharatiya Marathi Natya Sammelan chairs in this set: 2016 Thane — Jayant Savarkar (I); 2017 Osmanabad — Gangaram Gawankar (IV); 2018 Mulund — Premanand Gajvi (II); 2019 Nagpur — Kirti Shiledar (III).

subject: General Studies
question: Who can participate in the Government of India (MHRD) proposed IMPRINT-II scheme to inculcate culture of innovation among higher education institutes ? a. Professors in Private Colleges b. Professors in ITI c. Professors in IIT, NIT, IIIT d. Professors in IIT, NIT, IIIT, IISER and Central Universities
explanation: The right pick is option C. IMPRINT-II under MHRD opens participation to professors at IITs, NITs, and IIITs for industry-linked innovation — not private-college or ITI faculty, and in this key not the wider IISER/Central University pool in option (d).

subject: Polity
question: For economically backward classes, by the 103rd Constitutional Amendment in 2019, Article 15(6) and 16(6) of the Indian Constitution, following provisions are made. Choose the correct option. a. This reservation can be availed by persons not benefiting by schemes for SC, ST, OBC. b. The reservation proportion will be upto 13% for economically backward classes. c. This reservation is for education and job related benefits. d. The reservation proportion will be upto 10% for economically backward classes. Which of the above sentences are correct ?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. The 103rd Amendment (2019) Articles 15(6) and 16(6) reserve up to 10% for economically weaker sections in education and employment — statements (c) and (d); the 13% figure in (b) and the broader eligibility mix in other combos are excluded in this key.

subject: General Studies
question: For students belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Neo Buddhist class who did not get admission in the Government hostels, to enable them to take post matric education, the Government has started ________ for their lodging, boarding and educational facilities.

options.B: Bharat Ratna Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Swadhar Yojana

explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Maharashtra's Savitribai Phule Aadhar Yojana gives lodging, boarding, and educational support to SC/Neo-Buddhist students who miss government hostel seats; the Ambedkar Swadhar and other named schemes target different beneficiary groups.

subject: General Studies
question: Prof. Anil Gore, known as 'Marathi Kaka', was awarded State Government ________ award 2019 for popularising Marathi language.
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Prof Anil Gore ('Marathi Kaka') received the State Government's Poet V.V. Shirwadkar Award in 2019 for popularising Marathi; Tambe, Padgaonkar, and Khandekar awards honour other literary categories.

subject: General Studies
question: The Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO) will launch an unmanned campaign in December 2020.
explanation: The right pick is option A. ISRO's planned December 2020 unmanned precursor to crewed flight is named Gaganyaan in this question; Vyom Mitra, Robonaut, and Fedor are humanoid or foreign robot programmes, not the Indian mission title here.

subject: Polity
question: Consider the following statements about the 'Preamble' of the Indian Constitution : a. It states the objects which the Constitution seeks to establish and promote and also aids the legal interpretation of the Constitution where the language is found to be ambiguous. b. Like any other part of the Constitution, the 'Preamble' was not enacted by the Constituent Assembly.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Both Preamble statements stand in this key: it states constitutional objectives and aids interpretation when language is ambiguous (a), and the Preamble was not separately enacted outside the Constituent Assembly's work (b) as framed here.

subject: General Studies
question: Consider the following statements : a. It is a joint responsibility of the Sarpanch and Upa Sarpanch to maintain secured custody and proper safety of proceeding register and other relevant records of the Gram Sabha. b. The first meeting of the Gram Sabha in every financial year shall be held within two months from the commencement of that year.
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. Neither Gram Sabha statement holds: proceeding-register custody is not a joint Sarpanch–Upa-Sarpanch duty as (a) claims, and the first annual meeting rule in (b) is also wrong in this keyed pair — both statements are wrong together.

subject: Polity
question: Consider the following statements : a. Any resolution of Gram Panchayat shall be modified, amended, varied or cancelled by a Panchayat after a period of three months from the date of the passing thereof by another resolution supported by simple majority. b. No resolution of Gram Panchayat shall be modified, amended, varied or cancelled by a Panchayat within a period of three months from the date of the passing thereof, except by a resolution supported by two-third of the total number of members of such Panchayat.
explanation: The right pick is option C. Panchayat resolution rules in this set: after three months a simple majority can modify a resolution (a); within three months amendment needs a two-thirds majority of total membership (b) — both time-bound thresholds apply, not one alone.

subject: Reasoning
question: The judicial control over administrative actions emanates from the Doctrine of ________ .
explanation: The examiner has marked option C. Judicial control over administrative action is sourced in this MCQ to the Doctrine of Delegated Legislation; Judicial Review is the court's tool, Rule of Law the broader frame, and Separation of Powers a related structural principle.

subject: Economy
question: _____ यांनी नाशिक येथे 'ग्रंथोत्तेजक मंडळी' नावाची संस्था स्थापन केली होती.
explanation: सोडवत गेल्यास पर्याय B येतो. अधिकृत उत्तरतालिकेनुसार V. V. Shirwadkar (Kusumagraj) यांनी Nashik येथे 'Granthottejak Mandali' सुरू केली — Nashik च्या वाचनसंस्कृतीशी जोडलेले साहित्यिक मंडळ. Savarkar क्रांतिकारक राजकारण, Ranade व्यापक सुधारणा संस्था, Kanhere Muzaffarpur कट — या उत्तरतालिकेतील Nashik संबंध शी नाहीत.

subject: General Studies
question: First Lokpal of India is ________.
explanation: The right pick is option B. Justice T.S. Thakur is given as India's first Lokpal in this paper; Dipak Misra, Pinaki Chandra Ghose, and Khehar are associated with the Supreme Court bench, not this inaugural anti-corruption ombudsman post in the answer set.

subject: Economy
question: खालीलपैकी कोणत्या व्यक्तींनी प्रार्थना समाजाच्या माध्यमातून धार्मिक व सामाजिक सुधारणांचे कार्य केले होते ? अ. डॉ. आत्माराम पांडुरंग, डॉ. आर. जी. भांडारकर ब. वामन आबाजी मोडक, नारायण गणेश चंदावरकर क. विठ्ठल रामजी शिंदे, न्यायमूर्ती महादेव गोविंद रानडे ड. गोविंद विठ्ठल कुंटे, राव साहेब मंडलीक
explanation: येथे खात्रीशीर उत्तर पर्याय A. (a) Atmaram Pandurang व Bhandarkar, (b) Modak व Chandavarkar, (d) Kunte व Mandlik — उत्तरतालिकेतील यादीत Prarthana Samaj reform workers. (c) Shinde व Ranade वगळले — paper च्या grouping शी जुळवा, व्यापक reform roll-call नाही.

subject: Economy
question: 1885 ते 1915 या काळात _____ हे मुंबईचा अनभिषिक्त राजा म्हणून ओळखले जात.
explanation: थेट उत्तर — पर्याय C. 1885–1915 या काळात Dadabhai Naoroji ला 'अनभिषिक्त राजा' म्हणून उत्तरतालिका चिन्हांकित करते — Parsi leadership, economic drain thesis, Bombay presidency प्रभाव. Pherozeshah Mehta ला पाठ्यपुस्तके मध्ये अनेकदा हेच उपनाम; येथे उत्तरतालिका Naoroji कडे जाते.

explanation: योग्य उत्तर पर्याय C. Panchayat resolution — तीन महिने नंतर simple majority modify (a); तीन महिन्यांत two-thirds total membership (b) — दोन्ही time-bound thresholds, एकटे नाही.
